messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: When publication, how to display significant but direction uncertain structual equation?
parts: That depends on what you wish to depict. If B and C have no connection except through A, then use nothing between B and C. If there is residual covariance between B and C after accounting for the covariance due to their joining dependence on A, then convention represents that using a curved double-headed arrow. If you mean that B or C has an effect on the other, then use an arrow with one head.

parts: What if I kown there is a interaction between B and C

According to your graph, they are only outcomes, not predictors, so there is no basis for an "interaction" effect between them.  An interaction would imply they both predict another variable.  Are your arrows pointing in the wrong direction?  Should B and C be point to A (implying that they predict A, not the other way around)?
